data.narrative:
Solugen, a Series D climate and energy technology company, is evaluated against a comp universe of 9 private and 1 public peer in the Climate & Energy sector. The peer set spans similar and adjacent stages, anchored by Redwood Materials ($6.0B, Series D), KoBold Metals ($3.0B, Series C), Electric Hydrogen ($1.0B, Series C), and Amogy ($700M, Series C).

Two triangulation methods are applicable. Stage-progression methodology applies a 1.5x step-up multiplier to the $640M total raised proxy, implying a valuation of $960M. Peer-median analysis across the four comparable companies yields a median valuation of $2.0B, with a range spanning $700M to $6.0B. The stage-progression method anchors the lower end, while peer comparables—particularly Redwood Materials at Series D—support a higher valuation floor.

Triangulation of both methods supports a valuation range of $816M to $2.3B, with a median of $1.5B. The wide dispersion ($700M–$6.0B) in peer valuations reflects heterogeneity in technology maturity, capital intensity, and market perception within climate tech. Key uncertainties include Solugen's competitive positioning within this range relative to Redwood Materials and other Series D peers, capital efficiency versus comparables, and near-term de-risking milestones that would justify positioning toward the upper bound of the range.
